concept_summary: PAN-OS configuration uses XML-based hierarchical structure accessed via set commands similar to Junos. Initial setup includes hostname, management interface, admin accounts, and device registration. Configuration changes are staged in candidate config and require commit to activate. PAN-OS emphasizes security-first architecture with zones, policies, and application awareness as core concepts.
cli_mode_context: Enter configuration mode with 'configure'. Use 'set' commands to add configuration in XPath-like hierarchy. Use 'commit' to activate changes. GUI and CLI share XML configuration backend.
example_commands:
configure
set deviceconfig system hostname PA-NGFW-01
set deviceconfig system domain example.com
set deviceconfig system ip-address 192.0.2.10 netmask 255.255.255.0 default-gateway 192.0.2.1
set deviceconfig system dns-setting servers primary 8.8.8.8
set mgt-config users admin password
set deviceconfig system panorama-server 192.0.2.50
commit
run show system info

key_parameters.description: Executes operational mode commands from config mode

concept_summary: PAN-OS interfaces operate in Layer 3, Layer 2, virtual wire, or tap mode. Each interface is assigned to security zones for policy enforcement. Configuration includes IP addressing, virtual router assignment, and management profile for administrative access. Subinterfaces support VLAN tagging. Interface types include ethernet, loopback, tunnel, and aggregates.
cli_mode_context: Configure interfaces under 'set network interface ethernet'. Assign to zones under 'set zone'. Associate with virtual router under 'set network virtual-router'.
example_commands:
configure
set network interface ethernet ethernet1/1 layer3 ip 192.0.2.1/30
set network interface ethernet ethernet1/1 comment "WAN Uplink"
set network interface ethernet ethernet1/2 layer3 ip 198.51.100.1/24
set network interface ethernet ethernet1/2 comment "Internal LAN"
set zone untrust network layer3 ethernet1/1
set zone trust network layer3 ethernet1/2
set network virtual-router default interface [ethernet1/1 ethernet1/2]
set network interface ethernet ethernet1/3 layer3 units ethernet1/3.100 tag 100
set network interface ethernet ethernet1/3 layer3 units ethernet1/3.100 ip 203.0.113.1/24
commit

key_parameters.description: Sets interface to Layer 3 routed mode
Sets interface to Layer 2 switched mode
Assigns IP address with prefix length
Associates interface with VR for routing

concept_summary: PAN-OS supports VLANs through VLAN objects associated with Layer 2 interfaces or subinterfaces. Virtual wires provide transparent Layer 2 forwarding for inspection. VLAN interfaces enable inter-VLAN routing when assigned to zones with Layer 3 addressing. Layer 2 switching is limited compared to dedicated switches as PAN-OS focuses on security inspection.
cli_mode_context: Create VLAN objects under 'set network vlan'. Assign to Layer 2 interfaces or use subinterfaces with VLAN tags. Create VLAN interface for Layer 3 routing.
example_commands:
configure
set network vlan vlan100 virtual-interface interface vlan.100
set network interface vlan units vlan.100 ip 192.0.2.1/24
set zone trust network vlan vlan.100
set network vlan vlan100 interface ethernet1/5.100
set network interface ethernet ethernet1/5 layer2 units ethernet1/5.100 tag 100
set network virtual-router default interface vlan.100
commit

concept_summary: PAN-OS static routes are configured per virtual router with destination, next-hop, interface, and metric. Multiple virtual routers enable routing separation. Static routes support ECMP for load balancing. Route monitoring with BFD provides fast failure detection. Static routes integrate with path monitoring for conditional routing.
cli_mode_context: Configure static routes under 'set network virtual-router <name> routing-table ip static-route'. Specify destination, nexthop, interface, and metric.
example_commands:
configure
set network virtual-router default routing-table ip static-route default-route destination 0.0.0.0/0 nexthop ip-address 192.0.2.1 interface ethernet1/1
set network virtual-router default routing-table ip static-route lan-route destination 198.51.100.0/24 nexthop ip-address 203.0.113.1
set network virtual-router default routing-table ip static-route backup-route destination 0.0.0.0/0 nexthop ip-address 192.0.2.2 metric 20
set network virtual-router default routing-table ip static-route blackhole destination 203.0.113.128/25 nexthop discard
commit

concept_summary: PAN-OS supports OSPFv2 and OSPFv3 with area-based design per virtual router. Configuration includes router ID, areas, and interface participation. Authentication, route filtering, and redistribution integrate with security policies. OSPF routes are evaluated by security policy based on source/destination zones.
cli_mode_context: Configure OSPF under 'set network virtual-router <name> protocol ospf'. Define areas, enable on interfaces, set authentication and timers.
example_commands:
configure
set network virtual-router default protocol ospf enable yes
set network virtual-router default protocol ospf router-id 192.0.2.1
set network virtual-router default protocol ospf area 0.0.0.0 type normal
set network virtual-router default protocol ospf area 0.0.0.0 interface ethernet1/2 enable yes
set network virtual-router default protocol ospf area 0.0.0.0 interface ethernet1/2 link-type broadcast
set network virtual-router default protocol ospf area 0.0.0.0 interface ethernet1/2 metric 10
set network virtual-router default protocol ospf area 0.0.0.10 type normal
set network virtual-router default protocol ospf area 0.0.0.10 interface ethernet1/3.100 enable yes
commit

concept_summary: PAN-OS BGP supports IBGP and EBGP with peer groups and routing policies. Configuration per virtual router includes AS number, router ID, and peer definitions. Route filtering uses import/export policies. BGP integrates with App-ID for application-aware routing. Supports IPv4/IPv6 unicast and multicast address families.
cli_mode_context: Configure BGP under 'set network virtual-router <name> protocol bgp'. Define peer groups, neighbors, and routing policies.
example_commands:
configure
set network virtual-router default protocol bgp enable yes
set network virtual-router default protocol bgp router-id 192.0.2.1
set network virtual-router default protocol bgp local-as 65001
set network virtual-router default protocol bgp peer-group ebgp-peers type ebgp
set network virtual-router default protocol bgp peer-group ebgp-peers peer ISP-Peer peer-as 65002 local-address ip 192.0.2.1 peer-address ip 198.51.100.1
set network virtual-router default protocol bgp peer-group ibgp-peers type ibgp
set network virtual-router default protocol bgp peer-group ibgp-peers peer PE-Router local-address ip 192.0.2.1 peer-address ip 192.0.2.254
set network virtual-router default protocol bgp redist-rules default-route enable no
commit

key_parameters.description: Creates peer group (ebgp or ibgp type)

concept_summary: PAN-OS supports RIP for small networks with limited deployment. IS-IS and EIGRP are not supported as PAN-OS focuses on OSPF and BGP for dynamic routing. Route redistribution between protocols enables integration with existing networks. Policy-based forwarding provides alternative routing control.
cli_mode_context: Configure RIP under 'set network virtual-router <name> protocol rip' if needed. Most deployments use OSPF or BGP.
example_commands:
configure
set network virtual-router default protocol rip enable yes
set network virtual-router default protocol rip interface ethernet1/2 enable yes
set network virtual-router default protocol rip interface ethernet1/2 mode both
commit
reason: IS-IS and EIGRP are not supported on PAN-OS. RIP exists but limited. PAN-OS focus is security firewall with OSPF/BGP routing support, not comprehensive routing protocol suite.

concept_summary: PAN-OS provides high availability through active-passive or active-active clustering rather than VRRP/HSRP. HA pairs synchronize configuration, sessions, and routing information. Floating IP addresses provide gateway redundancy. HA links monitor cluster health with automatic failover. Virtual MAC addresses ensure seamless failover without ARP updates.
cli_mode_context: Configure HA under 'set deviceconfig high-availability'. Define peer IP, group ID, and monitoring settings.
example_commands:
configure
set deviceconfig high-availability interface ha1 ip-address 10.255.255.1 netmask 255.255.255.252
set deviceconfig high-availability interface ha1 port ethernet1/8
set deviceconfig high-availability interface ha2 ip-address 10.255.254.1 netmask 255.255.255.252
set deviceconfig high-availability interface ha2 port ethernet1/7
set deviceconfig high-availability group 1 mode active-passive
set deviceconfig high-availability group 1 peer-ip 10.255.255.2
set deviceconfig high-availability group 1 election-option device-priority 100
set deviceconfig high-availability group 1 election-option preemptive yes
set deviceconfig high-availability enabled yes
commit

key_parameters.description: Configures control link for HA communication
Configures data link for session sync
Enables preemption when higher priority recovers

concept_summary: PAN-OS security policies are core to traffic control using zone-based architecture. Policies match on zones, addresses, users, applications, and services. Each policy specifies action (allow, deny, drop) and security profiles (threat prevention, URL filtering, file blocking). Application-ID identifies traffic by behavior rather than just ports. Policy order matters with top-down evaluation.
cli_mode_context: Configure security policies under 'set rulebase security rules'. Create address objects and service objects for reusability. Organize in policy groups for management.
example_commands:
configure
set address LAN-Net ip-netmask 192.0.2.0/24
set address DMZ-Net ip-netmask 198.51.100.0/24
set service-group Web-Services members [service-http service-https]
set rulebase security rules Trust-to-Untrust from trust to untrust source LAN-Net destination any application any service application-default action allow
set rulebase security rules Trust-to-Untrust log-end yes
set rulebase security rules Block-Telnet from any to any source any destination any application telnet action deny
set rulebase security rules Block-Telnet log-start yes
set rulebase security rules DMZ-Inbound from untrust to dmz source any destination DMZ-Net application [ssl web-browsing] service application-default action allow
set rulebase security rules DMZ-Inbound profile-setting group default-security-profile
commit

concept_summary: PAN-OS NAT policies include source NAT, destination NAT, and static NAT with flexible translation options. NAT rules evaluate before security policies. Source NAT uses dynamic IP/port or static IP. Destination NAT enables port forwarding and load balancing. U-Turn NAT allows hairpinning. NAT policies support zone-based matching.
cli_mode_context: Configure NAT policies under 'set rulebase nat rules'. Define source and destination translation parameters. NAT policies are separate from security policies.
example_commands:
configure
set rulebase nat rules SNAT-Outbound source-translation dynamic-ip-and-port interface-address interface ethernet1/1 ip 198.51.100.1
set rulebase nat rules SNAT-Outbound from trust to untrust source 192.0.2.0/24 destination any
set rulebase nat rules DNAT-Web destination-translation translated-address 192.0.2.10 translated-port 443
set rulebase nat rules DNAT-Web from untrust to trust source any destination 198.51.100.50
set rulebase nat rules DNAT-Web service service-https
set rulebase nat rules Static-NAT source-translation static-ip translated-address 198.51.100.100 bi-directional yes
set rulebase nat rules Static-NAT from any to any source 192.0.2.20 destination any
commit

concept_summary: PAN-OS supports site-to-site IPsec VPN with IKEv1/IKEv2 and remote access VPN with GlobalProtect. Configuration includes IKE gateway, IPsec tunnel, and proxy IDs for traffic selectors. Route-based VPNs use tunnel interfaces while policy-based VPNs use proxy IDs. VPN integrates with security policies and zones. Supports certificate-based authentication.
cli_mode_context: Configure IKE gateway under 'set network ike gateway'. Configure IPsec tunnel under 'set network ike ipsec-tunnel'. Create tunnel interface and assign to zone. Add routes via tunnel.
example_commands:
configure
set network ike gateway Site-B-GW authentication pre-shared-key key MyPresharedKey123
set network ike gateway Site-B-GW protocol ikev2 dpd enable yes
set network ike gateway Site-B-GW protocol ikev2 ike-crypto-profile default
set network ike gateway Site-B-GW local-address ip 192.0.2.1 interface ethernet1/1
set network ike gateway Site-B-GW peer-address ip 203.0.113.1
set network ike ipsec-tunnel Site-B-Tunnel auto-key ike-gateway Site-B-GW
set network ike ipsec-tunnel Site-B-Tunnel auto-key ipsec-crypto-profile default
set network ike ipsec-tunnel Site-B-Tunnel tunnel-interface tunnel.1
set network interface tunnel units tunnel.1 ip 10.255.255.1/30
set zone vpn network layer3 tunnel.1
set network virtual-router default interface tunnel.1
set network virtual-router default routing-table ip static-route remote-lan destination 198.51.100.0/24 interface tunnel.1
commit

key_parameters.description: Defines IKE phase 1 parameters and peer
Logical tunnel interface for route-based VPN

concept_summary: PAN-OS QoS uses per-application bandwidth control and traffic shaping. QoS profiles define bandwidth guarantees and maximums per application or class. Traffic is classified by App-ID and assigned to classes. QoS policies apply to interfaces in egress direction. Priority queues support real-time traffic. Integration with SD-WAN provides application-aware path selection.
cli_mode_context: Create QoS profiles under 'set network qos profile'. Apply QoS to interfaces. Configure per-application bandwidth limits in QoS rules.
example_commands:
configure
set network qos profile Voice class 1 priority real-time
set network qos profile Voice class 1 bandwidth 30 percent guaranteed
set network qos profile Voice class 1 bandwidth 50 percent maximum
set network qos profile Data class 2 priority high
set network qos profile Data class 2 bandwidth 40 percent guaranteed
set network qos profile Default class 4 priority low
set network qos interface ethernet1/1 egress-max 100
set network qos interface ethernet1/1 qos-profile Voice
set rulebase qos rules Voice-Priority from trust to untrust application [sip voip] action class 1
commit

key_parameters.description: Defines QoS profile with traffic classes

concept_summary: PAN-OS supports local and external authentication using RADIUS, TACACS+, LDAP, SAML, or Kerberos. Admin authentication controls device access with role-based profiles. User-ID integrates with Active Directory for identity-based policies. Multi-factor authentication adds security. Authentication profiles map users to security policies for granular control.
cli_mode_context: Configure authentication profiles under 'set shared authentication-profile'. Define server profiles for RADIUS/TACACS+/LDAP. Assign to admin roles or firewall authentication.
example_commands:
configure
set shared server-profile radius RAD-Servers server Primary address 192.0.2.50 secret radiussecret123
set shared server-profile radius RAD-Servers server Secondary address 192.0.2.51 secret radiussecret123
set shared authentication-profile Auth-Profile method radius server-profile RAD-Servers
set shared authentication-profile Auth-Profile allow-list all
set shared administrator admin authentication-profile Auth-Profile
set shared admin-role NetworkOps role web-ui permit
set shared admin-role NetworkOps role cli permit
set shared administrator netadmin admin-role NetworkOps
set shared administrator netadmin authentication-profile Auth-Profile
commit

key_parameters.description: Defines custom admin role with permissions

concept_summary: PAN-OS supports SNMP v2c and v3 for monitoring with custom OIDs and standard MIBs. Logging sends to local storage, syslog, SNMP traps, or Panorama. Log types include traffic, threat, system, config, and HA. Severity filtering and forwarding profiles control log distribution. Integration with SIEMs through syslog. Panorama provides centralized log collection and correlation.
cli_mode_context: Configure SNMP under 'set deviceconfig system snmp-setting'. Configure logging under 'set shared log-settings'. Define syslog servers and profiles.
example_commands:
configure
set deviceconfig system snmp-setting access-setting version v2c snmp-community-string public123 access-type read-only
set deviceconfig system snmp-setting access-setting version v2c snmp-community-string public123 hosts 192.0.2.100
set deviceconfig system snmp-setting snmp-system contact netops@example.com
set deviceconfig system snmp-setting snmp-system location DataCenter-01
set shared log-settings syslog Syslog-Server server 192.0.2.200 transport UDP port 514 format BSD facility LOG_USER
set shared log-settings system match-list SendAll send-syslog Syslog-Server
set shared log-settings traffic match-list SendAll send-syslog Syslog-Server
set shared log-settings config match-list SendAll send-syslog Syslog-Server
commit

concept_summary: PAN-OS has limited native VXLAN support primarily for integration with data center fabrics. VM-Series in cloud and containerized deployments support VXLAN overlays. Physical appliances focus on security policy enforcement rather than VXLAN VTEP functionality. EVPN control plane is not a core PAN-OS feature.
cli_mode_context: VXLAN configuration is deployment-specific and limited. Typically handled by underlying infrastructure with PAN-OS providing security policy on top.
reason: VXLAN VTEP and EVPN control plane are not core features of PAN-OS. Palo Alto firewalls focus on security inspection and policy enforcement. VXLAN support exists for VM-Series cloud deployments but not as full data center fabric EVPN-VXLAN solution.

concept_summary: PAN-OS does not provide native MPLS PE router functionality as it is a security appliance platform. MPLS label inspection is supported for traffic visibility and security. SD-WAN features provide modern alternative to MPLS for WAN connectivity with application-aware routing and built-in security.
cli_mode_context: MPLS not directly configured. SD-WAN under 'set network virtual-router <name> ecmp' and SD-WAN plugin.
reason: MPLS L3VPN/L2VPN PE router functions are not PAN-OS capabilities. Palo Alto firewalls are security platforms, not service provider routers. SD-WAN features provide modern WAN connectivity alternative. MPLS label awareness exists for inspection but not forwarding/signaling.

concept_summary: PAN-OS HA provides active-passive or active-active clustering with session synchronization and configuration sync. HA pairs monitor health via heartbeat links with automatic failover. Active-active mode splits traffic by hash with symmetric return path enforcement. Preemption returns active role to higher priority device. Virtual MAC ensures seamless failover without ARP flux.
cli_mode_context: Configure HA under 'set deviceconfig high-availability'. Define interfaces, mode, peer addressing, and monitoring parameters.
example_commands:
configure
set deviceconfig high-availability interface ha1 ip-address 10.255.255.1 netmask 255.255.255.252
set deviceconfig high-availability interface ha1 port ethernet1/8
set deviceconfig high-availability interface ha1-backup ip-address 192.0.2.201 netmask 255.255.255.0
set deviceconfig high-availability interface ha1-backup port ethernet1/1
set deviceconfig high-availability interface ha2 ip-address 10.255.254.1 netmask 255.255.255.252
set deviceconfig high-availability interface ha2 port ethernet1/7
set deviceconfig high-availability interface ha2-backup ip-address 10.255.253.1 netmask 255.255.255.252
set deviceconfig high-availability interface ha2-backup port ethernet1/6
set deviceconfig high-availability group 1 mode active-passive
set deviceconfig high-availability group 1 peer-ip 10.255.255.2
set deviceconfig high-availability group 1 election-option device-priority 100
set deviceconfig high-availability group 1 election-option preemptive yes
set deviceconfig high-availability group 1 election-option heartbeat-backup yes
set deviceconfig high-availability group 1 monitoring link-monitoring enabled yes
set deviceconfig high-availability group 1 monitoring link-monitoring link ethernet1/1 enabled yes
set deviceconfig high-availability enabled yes
commit

key_parameters.description: Control link for HA state synchronization
Enables preemption when higher priority recovers
Monitors interface health for failover trigger

concept_summary: PAN-OS system management includes configuration backup via export, software upgrades with dynamic updates, and certificate management. Panorama provides centralized management for multiple firewalls. Configuration commits create revision history with rollback capability. Content updates include threat signatures, applications, and URL databases. CLI and GUI share XML configuration backend.
cli_mode_context: Use 'save config' to export configuration. Use 'load config' to import. Software management through 'request system software' commands. Panorama managed devices sync config automatically.
example_commands:
configure
set deviceconfig system panorama-server 192.0.2.50
set deviceconfig system panorama-server 192.0.2.51
commit
exit
save config to backup-config.xml
load config from backup-config.xml
request system software check
request system software download version 11.1.2
request system software install version 11.1.2
request restart system
show system software status
show config list
request commit-lock add comment "Maintenance window"
request commit-lock remove
debug software restart process management-server
